static_traits.name: Hai Li
static_traits.social_status: Has friends and colleagues to discuss work stress with, but has not shared the strong thoughts of wanting to quit; relationships with colleagues are affected by stress and negative thinking
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problems in the past, has not received psychotherapy, no major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, relatively good logic; neutral attitude, cooperative; able to self-reflect, but tends to use 'should' statements and focus on negative details

basic_info.main_problem: Although I love party planning work, being around crowds and tight deadlines for a long time leaves me feeling overwhelmed and exhausted, with frequent thoughts of quitting (intensified about 6 months ago in a high-pressure large-event situation).
basic_info.core_demands: 'I want to regain my love for work, and no longer always feel overwhelmed.'
growth_experiences: Six months ago, the client needed to plan a large event with a tight deadline and high expectations, triggering marked stress and anxiety; afterward, feelings of being overwhelmed and negative thoughts appeared at work almost every day, gradually affecting sleep and eating, and leading to reduced performance and strained relationships with colleagues.
Family-of-origin background: the father was once a member of the Communist Party (specific influence not mentioned).

core_beliefs: I am not suited for this job
If I cannot handle stress better, it proves I am not good enough

special_situations.event: When planning a large event, facing a pressing deadline and high expectations.
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot cope perfectly under high pressure, it means I am incompetent and will fail.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Sets strict self-demands ('I should be able to withstand pressure better'), works overtime and forces themselves to work harder; occasionally rests briefly but considers it ineffective.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am not suited for this job; I will never be competent at it.

special_situations.event: During event planning and execution, needing long-term close contact with large crowds.
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I am constantly in contact with people I will be drained; I should be able to handle interpersonal and social demands all the time, otherwise I do not deserve this job.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces revealing true feelings to others, only taking brief rests for relief, but with limited effect.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Being surrounded by crowds makes me want to quit; I cannot hold on anymore.

special_situations.event: Last week's event was overall very successful, but a few problems occurred.
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: As long as any mistake occurs, it means I have failed and am not good enough.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Excessively focusing on what went wrong and ignoring positive outcomes and performance.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Although it was fine overall, I still messed it up.

special_situations.event: When feeling overwhelmed, recalling work performance and stress tolerance.
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I must / should be able to withstand pressure better and maintain perfect performance, otherwise I am not qualified.
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reproaching oneself with strict standards, negating existing effort and progress.
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should have been able to handle this stress better long ago.

core_conflict.wish: Desires to be recognized in the work they love, to maintain competence and a sense of control, while not being excessively swallowed by interpersonal matters and stress
core_conflict.fear: Fears failure and not being recognized, fears being depleted by high pressure and dense interpersonal demands to the point of losing the self and ability
defense_goal: Maintaining control and avoiding failure evaluation by raising standards and self-reproach
Reducing disclosure of real difficulties to others to avoid being seen as incompetent

object_relations.self_representation: A practitioner who is not good enough and easily crushed by stress
object_relations.object_representation: A group/colleagues/clients with high expectations, demanding and will judge oneself

object_relations.self_representation: 需要独自扛压的工作者
object_relations.object_representation: Others who cannot understand one's real difficulties (friends/colleagues)

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor proposes focusing on the positive and trying a new exercise (such as recording three things done well)
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Tends to think change is hard and practice may be 'of little use', in order to avoid facing stronger emotional fluctuations and possible failure
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Expresses doubt in a polite, gentle, and reserved tone, such as 'I am not sure whether it will help'; emphasizes concrete steps and feasibility, not going deeply into the emotional level for now.

manifestations: Love for the work is overshadowed by stress and negative filtering, making it hard to experience value and meaning
Frequently producing thoughts of resigning, doubting one's competence

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Frequently uses the self-demand 'I should be able to handle stress better'
Uses perfect performance as a rigid standard for measuring self-worth

contact_model.definition: The individual has a poor capacity for self-reflection and introspection, with excessive self-restriction and self-blame, and is overly cautious about contact, corresponding to 'autonomy'.
manifestations: Excessive vigilance about and harsh criticism of one's own performance at work
Unwilling to fully express to friends the true extent of wanting to resign

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or objects, or gives up seeking others to do something for them and instead does it to themselves; that is, the individual redirects energy originally intended outward toward themselves, corresponding to 'impulse'.
manifestations: Reducing outward seeking of emotional support; internalizing stress and digesting it alone
Turning the impulse to express outwardly into self-blame and self-demands

exception_events.target_problem: Under the high-pressure situations of event planning and execution, the client usually focuses only on the negative and concludes they are not competent, then wants to quit, with declining performance.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Last week the client planned a 'great' event, with a good overall outcome; despite a few minor issues, compared with past worries, the objective performance showed that the client is competent.
exception_events.reason: Clues: this event was overall successful (the client described it as 'great'), indicating that their existing skills and experience can support good performance.

positive_force: 对派对策划有热情与投入
Having the ability to be competent at work (recent overall successful event)
Having some support network of friends and colleagues
Proactively seeking help, willing to try to change
negative_force: Predicting failure and self-negation ('I will never succeed')
Rigid 'should' self-demands lead to increased stress
Exhaustion from long-term intensive interpersonal contact
Concealing real troubles, reducing access to external support

target_behavior.behavior: When planning and executing events, marked anxiety and exhaustion appear, accompanied by negative automatic thoughts and self-reproach such as 'I am not suited for this job' and 'I will never succeed', and frequent urges to quit arise
antecedent: High expectations and tight deadlines for a large event
长时间与多人密集互动
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjected rigid standards and negative cognitive biases (negative filtering, catastrophizing / predicting failure, 'should' statements) lead the client to equate the experience of stress with self-evaluations of failure and incompetence
target_behavior.function: Escapes unwelcome things (failure and others' evaluations), obtaining short-term relief and emotional easing through thoughts of quitting
target_behavior.consequence: Work performance declined, sleep and eating affected, relationships with colleagues strained, enthusiasm for work and sense of meaning reduced, persistent thoughts of quitting
